references.text: Warns against having an evil eye toward the poor, linking to the theme of a jealous or stingy gaze
Refers to one who has an evil eye and chases after wealth, related to the evil eye toward the poor brother
Uses the same term 'belial' (wickedness/worthlessness) in connection with the heart
The context of the year of release (shemitta) mentioned in the verse
Warns against sinning by withholding wages from the poor, who will cry out to the Lord
Warns against oppressing the poor, for they will cry out to God and it will be a sin
Jesus teaches about the evil eye in contrast to the good eye, related to generosity and stinginess
The question of the evil eye because the master is generous, linking to jealousy over others' blessings
One who knows how to do good but does not do it, for him it is sin - parallel to refusing help to those in need
One who has earthly goods and sees his brother in distress but closes his heart, a question about God's love
